Mason Mount’s availability for the trip to Hull is in the balance due to a knock.

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for as the new season kicks off
Sports.content:
1 Nwaneri out of Arsenal picture

While Myles Lewis-Skelly looks likely to remain at the Emirates, the same can’t be said for Ethan Nwaneri. The 19-year-old was outstanding in his breakthrough season for Arsenal in 2024-25 but barely featured last season and was sent on loan to Marseille. That didn’t really work out and Arsenal are now exploring another temporary move to ensure Nwaneri gets regular football this season. Milan, RB Leipzig, Dortmund and Fulham are all thought to be interested, with Nwaneri unlikely to feature on the bench for Friday’s opener against Coventry as a result. Whether Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus are available remains to be seen as Arsenal attempt to find suitors for the Brazil duo. Ed Aarons

Arsenal v Coventry City, Friday 8pm (all times BST)

2 New United pair down for Tigers test

Manchester United’s summer transfer business has focused on recruiting in central midfield. It will be interesting to see who Michael Carrick selects in two key roles for the first game of the season. Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have been present for more of pre-season than Kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute for England at the World Cup and was a late returner to Carrington after a holiday. Carlos Baleba surely will not have arrived in time to start at Hull. Mainoo is in the best position in the long term but if Carrick decides to ease him into the season, it would be intriguing to see how Santos and Tielemans team up, the stress test for a new partnership that could provide the perfect balance of defensive awareness and ability to move the team up the pitch. Will Unwin

Hull City v Manchester United, Saturday 12.30pm

3 Can Ipswich copy Black Cats’ success?

Ipswich clearly learned a lot from what Sunderland did a year ago, as they went out and bought a lot of players. The Black Cats quickly moulded their 19 acquisitions into a successful unit but at least they had the positive of a head coach in Régis Le Bris who had his feet under the table. Gary O’Neil is the new man at Portman Road and he has 12 signings – at time of writing – to potentially use for the opener. The record arrival, Emersonn, who has moved to Portman Road from Toulouse, is the most eye-catching of those who have been acquired. The Brazilian has an underwhelming career goalscoring record and a few question marks hanging over his head. Even though it is their first game, Ipswich need to pick up points at home, and to do so require a striker who can cause problems for defenders. How quickly Emersonn adapts will be critical for the Tractor Boys’ success this year. WU

Ipswich Town v Sunderland, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen Emersonn is one of a number of big-money signings made by promoted Ipswich this summer. Photograph: Keeran Marquis/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

4 Glasner’s tough Diomande ready for debut

August is the season for debuts and no one will be more satisfied than Oliver Glasner when Ousmane Diomande steps over the white line at the City Ground. Glasner wanted the Ivorian centre-back to replace Marc Guéhi at Crystal Palace, six months before the England defender departed for Manchester City. Diomande, a £34m buy from Sporting, is expected to line up in a back three for Nottingham Forest against Leeds, when the Austria midfielder Xaver Schlager, who played for Glasner at Wolfsburg, could also make his Forest bow. Diomande is a quick and physical defender but another aspect of his appeal is his aerial power at set pieces. “They’ve both played Champions League football and they are used to competing for titles,” said Glasner. “They can add this winning mentality.” Ben Fisher

Nottingham Forest v Leeds, Saturday 3pm

5 Serene Senesi can bring calm to Spurs

Cristian Romero has taken his maverick brand of defending to Atlético Madrid, upsetting neutral Premier League watchers. His compatriot Marcos Senesi has arrived to shore up things at the back as Roberto De Zerbi desperately tries to steer Spurs away from a third straight season of battling relegation. The all-action Romero had his qualities as a leader and defender but never felt dependable, which is what most want from a centre-back and captain. Senesi impressed during his time at Bournemouth, rarely making headlines but proving himself a calm presence at the back. The Argentinian is good on the ball and will be more adventurous in possession than his countryman. He is yet to be sent off in three seasons as a Premier League player – Romero was dismissed twice in 2025-26 alone, not to mention a one-match ban and a fine for his behaviour towards a referee. His calmness will improve Spurs. WU

Brentford v Tottenham, Saturday 5.30pm

6 Villa head south besieged by problems

It is surely not how Unai Emery envisaged the countdown to Aston Villa’s season-opener at Brighton on Sunday – and certainly not as he enjoyed the afterglow from the club’s Europa League triumph over Freiburg in May. The manager has an extraordinary number of problems. Take the midfield where the new signings João Gomes and Johan Manzambi are injury doubts. Note: Amadou Onana is a long-term casualty while Youri Tielemans has been sold. It goes on. Emery is about to lose Ezri Konsa to Arsenal – in a summer where Villa have also sold Morgan Rogers and Lucas Digne. They are trying to move on Emi Martínez, while the future of Ollie Watkins is uncertain, with Al-Hilal circling. For the cherry on top, the rampaging 17-year-old striker Brian Madjo is a fitness concern. Emery’s teamsheet will be very interesting. Will he pitch the new goalkeeper, Zion Suzuki, who only signed on Wednesday, straight in? David Hytner

Brighton v Aston Villa, Sunday 2pm

7 Maresca must win to silence City noise

Is Enzo Maresca already under pressure after Manchester City’s 3-0 schooling by Arsenal in the Community Shield? Maybe not, but if the Italian’s new team go down at home to Bournemouth on Sunday, you do not have to be a soothsayer to picture the scrutiny that will follow. Maresca and City are enduring a difficult transfer window, with Rodri’s departure to Barcelona the headline, a dizzying blow that has to be shaken off. The new Bournemouth coach, Marco Rose, has faced City six times in the Champions League with Leipzig and Mönchengladbach, and is sure to order his visitors to go for the jugular at the Etihad. City are vulnerable but Maresca can remedy this with a win of any sort. This, after all, is the job many felt he was the obvious choice for. Jamie Jackson

Manchester City v Bournemouth, Sunday 2pm

View image in fullscreen Anything but a win for Manchester City at home to Bournemouth will increase scrutiny on Enzo Maresca. Photograph: Dimitris Legakis/EPA

8 King Kev remembered at Newcastle

Kevin Keegan was supposed to have been the guest of honour at St James’ Park on Sunday, but his death from cancer in July means this meeting of two of his old clubs will turn into a tribute to one of English football’s enduring heroes. Keegan’s family will be present to witness an outpouring of love for the former Liverpool and Newcastle forward and (twice) Magpies manager. Once the game kicks off, all eyes will be on Alexander Isak, a St James’ Park old boy whose decision to force a £125m move to Anfield last summer did not go down well on Tyneside. The Sweden striker, making his first return to Newcastle, has much to prove at Liverpool, and now has a new head coach to impress in Andoni Iraola. Newcastle too have a new face in the home dugout, where Matthias Jaissle will occupy the technical area for so long inhabited by Eddie Howe. Louise Taylor

Newcastle v Liverpool, Sunday 4.30pm

9 Former Madrid managers meet in capital

Real Madrid’s two head coaches from last season meet at Craven Cottage, with the focus on Xabi Alonso, rather than Álvaro Arbeloa. The Fulham man, however, may have more to prove in the Premier League. His managerial career has been less prominent than that of his Basque rival – and he has clearly insisted on snapping up talent from the Bernabéu. Gonzalo García and César Palacios have made the trip over from the Spanish capital with Arbeloa. It shows great faith from the former Liverpool defender but it does put extra pressure on the trio, their fates now permanently intertwined. All three need a positive start to show they merit being in the Premier League. Otherwise, it would be very easily to criticise them individually and collectively. WU

Sports.title: Ronaldinho, 46, on mission of love and happiness – and maybe goals – at Serie C’s Ravenna
Sports.content:
It seemed like a joke, a hoax, when at 10pm on 19 June, Ravenna broke the news of Ronaldinho’s signing. The Brazilian, a former Ballon d’Or winner and one of the most recognisable figures in world football, had played his last official match in 2015 for Fluminense; a professional signing in Serie C at 46 years of age seemed unrealistic, to say the least. With football’s attention taken by the World Cup, the game was shocked by this bolt from the blue. For the most part, it remained in disbelief.

There was much discussion, in the city and around the world, about the real value of this operation, and we talked about it too, speaking with the mayor, the fans, and the president of Ravenna, Ignazio Cipriani, scion of the family known globally for Harry’s Bar, who is giving his city much more than a dream.

A dream that materialised, dispelling any doubts, at 11.50am on Thursday, when Ronaldinho, in a floral shirt and Bermuda shorts, with his now-familiar flat cap on his head, walked down the steps of the private jet that brought him from Milan Linate to the runway of Forlì airport. It is all true, all real. From there, he went on to the customary medical, like a true footballer. Ronaldinho is becoming a partner in the Ravenna club, as explained by the president, but he will also do his part on the pitch, with the dream of scoring the final goal of his career in the yellow-and-red jersey.

Then came the quick press conference, organised by the ownership at the Monaldina, the historic residence of the Gardini-Ferruzzi entrepreneurial family, the maternal dynasty from which Cipriani descends. There were few questions and hushed answers, very few words carefully chosen by Ronaldinho, who with his customary smile and gentle manners truly seems to have stepped back in time.

“The Milan derby is the most beautiful memory of my previous Italian experience,” began the former Barcelona and Milan No 10, before clarifying what drove him to Romagna: “Friendship and passion are the keys that brought me back here.”

He then clarified his goals in Ravenna: “To help, to excite the other players, and to have a spectacular season. To win, if possible.” Regarding his possible presence on the pitch, he explained: “If a goal comes, my experience in Ravenna will become even more beautiful, but whether I will actually play will be decided by the president and the coach.”

What does he think of the enthusiasm of Ravenna, a city that has literally gone crazy for him? Ronaldinho smiled and replied: “I just arrived, but I have a great desire to live this experience with the whole city.” His mission, he had already declared, is to bring happiness and love.

Echoing his words and capturing the essence of the city’s excitement was Ariedo Braida. Almost enunciating every word, the veteran executive summarised the operation with a striking remark: “We have the magic of football in Ravenna, what more could we ask for?”

View image in fullscreen Ronaldinho salutes onlookers but he will not participate in Ravenna’s opening Serie C game on Monday. Photograph: Massimo Paolone/LaPresse/Shutterstock

The former Milan and Barcelona director also recalled the opinion expressed by Kevin-Prince Boateng in 2016, according to which Ronaldinho holds the top spot in a ranking that also includes Pelé, Maradona, Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo.

Closing the circle was Cipriani himself, who revealed the behind-the-scenes of the miracle, after clarifying: “Ronaldinho is in shape.” When asked how he convinced the Brazilian champion, the answer was identical to that of the player: “Friendship and passion.” Cipriani then confirmed Ronaldinho’s entry as a shareholder in Ravenna FC, insisting on the profound meaning of the corporate move: “It’s not just about marketing, it’s not just international visibility. It is the chance to create a new enthusiasm around the club and the yellow-and-red jersey.”

Then the party began, organised in grand style on a stage set up on the beach at Marina di Ravenna, featuring the presentation of the entire Ravenna squad. The club’s president does not hide the ambition of a rapid climb to Serie B, with his sights set on the top flight. The star of the event, needless to say, was the Brazilian star, who for the first time presented himself before his new people, those Ravenna fans who back in June were curious, sceptical, or in disbelief.

Every doubt was dispelled on the beach of the ancient Byzantine capital, which today, with the arrival of the former Ballon d’Or winner, can truly dream big.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In living memory, the Romagnol city has never been talked about so much all over the world.

View image in fullscreen Ronaldinho’s unexpected comeback has captured fans’ imaginations, with 2,700 season tickets sold. Photograph: Stefano Rellandini/AFP/Getty Images

The fans didn’t just show up on the beach to celebrate their new idol, they also did so at the box office: the “Ronaldinho effect” has led to over 2,700 season tickets sold for Ravenna’s Serie C campaign, which kicks off on Monday in Reggio Emilia.

Ronaldinho, as confirmed by Cipriani, will not take part in the away match, but the fans hope to soon see him wearing the No 10 jersey, which was handed to him upon his arrival in Ravenna by the head coach, Andrea Mandorlini.

“Thank you very much,” are the words Ronaldinho dedicated to his celebrating people, while a child climbing the scaffolding of the giant screen shouted: “I saw him!”

He saw him at 46 years old, they had told him stories about him. Perhaps he will see him play again. This is the magic of football.

Sports.title: ‘Just boring’ – Premier League club told to make Jack Grealish and Liam Delap double swoop or risk relegation fight
Sports.content:
Everton have been told to become less 'boring' in the transfer market and make an ambitious double swoop for Jack Grealish and Liam Delap.

The Toffees have made five summer signings thus far, although they've gone under the radar with the total fees amounting to £74million.

4 Everton have been warned they won't improve on their 13th place Premier League finish lasts season unless they take drastic action in the transfer market Credit: PA

And former Everton defender Ashley Williams feels they need to show more ambition in the transfer window and said the best they can hope for is a 13th place finish in the Premier League table as things stand.

"I just think it's a little bit boring," Williams said on Kick Off about Everton's summer window. "If you're an Everton fan, it's so boring at the minute. Everyone else around you is talking about incomings, outgoings, what you're trying to do.

"What are Everton trying to do? I don't get it. The best thing they could hope for is 13th again this season. They're not going to improve on that with the squad they've got.

"They've brought in a couple of players. They're not going to get you any higher at all.

"You still don't really have a striker. You've lost Seamus Coleman, which is never mind right-back position, just what you've lost in the dressing room is massive.

"It's just a lack of ambition that I'm seeing from Everton at the minute. You've just moved into this massive, unreal stadium that you're trying to call home.

"David Moyes did an excellent job to steady that first season in a new stadium, which we've seen be difficult before. Yes, it's not the most expansive and attractive football to watch, but they didn't need that last season. They just needed to be a stable club.

"They didn't need to get into Europe last season. They're not ready for that at all. But this season, you're stable, you're in a new stadium, you did a good job. Now let's see, let's show a bit of ambition to do something. Get the fans a little bit excited for that first game of the season.

"Well, with all due respect, Christian Norgaard, Merlin Rohl, Hayden Hackney, they're not getting the fans excited at all. There's still no striker. You've got Beto and Thierno Barry. They're not going to take you any higher than 13th."

Everton urged to make Delap move

Williams then urged the Merseyside club to pursue striker Liam Delap with Chelsea keen to offload the former Ipswich man.

4 Nottingham Forest are frontrunners to sign Delap but Williams wants to see Everton put a bid in Credit: Getty

"Bring some people in the door," Williams added. Liam Delap, go and get him. Do everything you can do now to go and get him through the door because he needs a team that want him.

"Throw everything at him. I don't understand why. I really don't get what they're doing. It sounds a little bit like David Moyes doesn't really get the direction either.

"I'm guessing he's given them targets. Surely these are the players I want. This is the type of profile of player I want.

"They haven't delivered on anything. There's nothing to talk about. The fans have got nothing to talk about. It's just boring for them at the moment."

Everton also told to sign Grealish

Presenter Natalie Sawyer also suggested another English star whose future remains unclear in Grealish as a player Everton could try and re-sign before the September 1 deadline.

"Absolutely. I'd snap your hand off for Jack Grealish right now because he's the type of they need quality players like him to enjoy," Williams responded.

4 Grealish spent last season on loan at Everton and is in the final year of his Manchester City contract Credit: Getty

"I do like what he needs to up his actual productivity. But if you if they can get Jack Grealish back in as well as others, you absolutely take him."

Everton warned about relegation fight

While Williams and fellow pundit Lianne Sanderson don't believe Everton will get relegated, they've been warned that the season could be an uncomfortable one.

"I don't think they'll go down but they'll be down amongst it," Sanderson said.

"Barry scored eight goals last year and Iliman Ndiaye scored six. That's nowhere near good enough. They need someone that can put the ball in the back of the net, but my concern is in the midfield.

"New stadium. It's fantastic, the Evertonians are so passionate... I think when you don't strengthen, and maybe that's David Moyes' frustration.

"I liked David Moyes when he was at West Ham and I know West Ham fans used to call in the show and hammer me, no pun intended, because they used to say his style of football was no good. So sometimes you have to be careful what you wish for.

4 Everton have brought in one of the stars of last season's Championship in Hayden Hackney, but the Kick Off panel aren't inspired by these signings Credit: Getty

Yes, his style might not be great, but when you look at that squad, it doesn't excite me at all. They haven't strengthened... I think they're going to struggle."

Everton's transfer business

Moyes has spent £24m each on the acquisition of Hackney from Middlesbrough as well as winger Tyrique George from Chelsea.

German midfielder Rohl arrived from Freiburg in a £19m deal while Norgaard joined from Arsenal in a cut-price £7m switch.

Forward Brennan Johnson has walked through the door in a swap deal which has seen Dwight McNeil go to Crystal Palace.

Everton begin their campaign with a clash against Crystal Palace on Saturday at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Sports.title: Liverpool have Bradley Barcola alternative staring them in the face and he is half the price
Sports.content:
Liverpool have Bradley Barcola alternative staring them in the face and he is half the price

Liverpool have the perfect Bradley Barcola alternative staring them in the face this summer, according to Andy Brassell.

He believes that Barcola's teammate Ibrahim Mbaye would represent a very handy option should a deal for Barcola not prove to be possible.

5 Barcola is set to depart Paris Saint-Germain this summer after a host of attacking arrivals Credit: AFP

talkSPORT understands that the French international wants to move to Anfield this summer.

However, the Reds are unwilling to match the asking price.

Paris Saint-Germain are asking for around £130million to part ways with Barcola despite the club signing a few new forwards.

Mbaye has reportedly agreed personal terms with Liverpool as well and could be part of a double deal.

But if not, Brassell feels as if Mbaye would make more sense than Barcola.

Speaking exclusively to talkSPORT.com's Lead Features Writer Joe Brophy, Brassell praised Mbaye.

He said: "I think he's an enormous young talent who needs to get out and play. And he won't do that in Paris."

When asked if a move to Liverpool made sense, he responded: "It could be. Although, obviously, if we frame it like that, replacing Salah directly, well, A, is impossible. But B, that's a lot of pressure to put on someone.

"In terms of the fact that they need a right-sided forward, I think they need a right-sided forward more than they need Bradley Barcola.

"Not that I think Bradley Barcola would be anything less than excellent for them. But, yeah, that's definitely the key spot that they need to replace. And obviously, they're going around the squad and making little upgrades.

"And really, I think Liverpool are still settling from last year's transfer window, which was a bit tumultuous, really.

"A lot more change than a lot of people expected. But, yeah, a right-side player and a right-side player of talent is exactly what they need."

5 Mbaye is a special young talent and full Senegalese international already

5 Barcola is still Liverpool's top target as the transfer window ticks towards its conclusion Credit: Getty

Double departure

PSG have signed three attacking players in the transfer window.

Maghned Akliouche has arrived from Monaco to slot in as an option on the right.

Mika Godts has swapped Ajax for Paris to be a left winger for Luis Enrique's side, and Ferran Torres has also come in.

So, some players need to leave, and Brassell can see both Barcola and Mbaye departing.

"Yeah, absolutely. And I don't think it's just down to the Trophy de Champions [where they were both out of the squad]. I think, really, if something has happened this weekend, to mean that it's in the best interest of everyone for Barcola and Mbaye to move, which I think it was anyway, it's the fact that you've got that incredible front three and then you've added Akliouche to that.

"And over this weekend, on Friday, they added Ferran Torres, officially, at last. And then they've added Mika Godts as well. So, that really squeezes the minutes for the other guys, I think. And that really indicates that PSG are ready to do business before the bell tolls on September 1st.

"And we've seen that PSG earlier in this window have sold very well. I think they'll continue to sell very well. That's a huge part of being an elite club, isn't it?"

5 Andoni Iraola is after some more attacking additions Credit: Getty

Mbaye's rise

Despite being just 18, Mbaye is already an established player for Senegal.

He has four goals for his country, including one during the 2026 World Cup.

Last year was his big breakthrough in Ligue 1 as he made 24 appearances for the French giants, racking up some very good minutes.

He grabbed three goals and two assists and also appeared in the Champions League four times as well.

So, he's had one year of first-team football, but the talent is undoubtedly there, and he is a right winger, which Liverpool absolutely need.

5 Mbaye is a top talent who could thrive in the Premier League Credit: Getty

Liverpool's transfer window so far

The Reds have seen a summer of upheaval.

Mohamed Salah and Andrew Robertson have departed the club, with Curtis Jones set to join them as well.

He's heading to Inter Milan, while Cody Gakpo continues to be linked with Tottenham Hotspur.

Ibrahima Konate also didn't sign a new contract and has joined Real Madrid.

Jeremy Jacquet has arrived to replace Konate, and Julian Araujo is in on loan from Barcelona.

And there has only been one further addition, with Victor Munoz joining from Osasuna.

So, plenty still to do for Andoni Iraola.

Sports.title: EFL player handed retrospective two-match ban after handball goal in first of its kind ruling
Sports.content:
EFL player handed retrospective two-match ban after handball goal in first of its kind ruling

West Brom striker Aune Heggebo has been handed a two-match ban by the FA in a 'first of its kind' ruling.

The forward has been suspended for 'successfully deceiving a match official' in his side's controversial 2-1 win over Norwich City.

4 Heggebo has been handed a two-match ban by the FA for his handball goal against Norwich Credit: Alamy

Heggebo scored the Baggies' opening goal in their away victory at Carrow Road on Saturday.

However, replays showed he had diverted Jimmy-Jay Morgan's cross into the net with his arms.

Despite the appeals of the Norwich players, the goal was allowed to stand by referee Tim Robinson.

The goal quickly went viral on social media, leading to calls for VAR to be introduced by the EFL.

FA statement

Following the incident, Heggebo was subsequently charged by the FA this week.

Despite West Brom appealing against their decision, he has been suspended for two matches with immediate effect.

Confirming the punishment in a statement, the FA spokesperson said: "West Bromwich Albion’s Aune Heggebo has been given a two-match ban for successful deception of a match official during their EFL Championship match against Norwich City on Saturday 15 August.

"It was alleged that the player acted in an improper manner in or around the 75th minute of the match, whereby he successfully deceived a match official by handling the ball in a direct and successful attempt to score a goal, contrary to FA Rule E3.1.

"Aune Heggebo denied the charge against him, however an independent Regulatory Commission found it to be proven and imposed this sanction following a hearing.

"The Regulatory Commission’s written reasons will be published in due course."

4 Heggebo was charged for 'successfully deceiving a match official' after scoring with his arms Credit: Getty

Heggebo will now miss Sunday's home match against Burnley, live on talkSPORT 2.

The 25-year-old will also be suspended for West Brom's trip to Newcastle United in the Carabao Cup second round on Wednesday.

He will be available to return to action away at Middlesbrough on Saturday, August 29.

West Brom statement

West Brom have released a statement of their own following the ban, confirming their plans to seek clarification from the FA.

The club will request guidance on how their players should react in future to avoid a repeat offence.

In a statement, the Baggies said: "The FA on Tuesday charged Heggebo with a breach of Rule E3.1 in relation to his goal at Norwich City on Saturday.

4 West Brom will seek clarity from the FA after an unsuccessful appeal against the charge Credit: Getty

"The charge is believed to be the first of its kind in English football, following a rule change prior to the 2024/25 season.

"The FA alleged Heggebo did 'successfully deceive a Match Official by handling the ball in a direct successful attempt to score a goal'.

"Albion appealed on Wednesday, stating the ball took a deflection from the goalkeeper immediately before making contact with Heggebo's arm, which materially affected the ball's trajectory and left him with less than 0.1 of a second to react.

"Given the accidental nature of the handball, the club argued it could not be reasonably viewed as a deliberate act of deception.

"On Thursday, the matter was placed before a Regulatory Commission, which upheld the charge.

"The club will now write to the FA requesting clarification on how a player is reasonably expected to react should similar circumstances arise in the future.

4 Heggebo will miss West Brom's matches against Burnley and Newcastle Credit: Getty

"Albion remain steadfast in their support of Aune, whose character and integrity have been evident throughout his time at The Hawthorns."

Heggebo joined the Baggies from Brann in his native Norway last summer.

He has since scored ten goals in 47 Championship appearances for the club.

James Morrison's side sit fourth in the second-tier following their opening weekend win over the Canaries.

Sports.title: Aston Villa have £20m bid to sign England international as potential Ezri Konsa replacement rejected
Sports.content:
Aston Villa have £20m bid to sign England international as potential Ezri Konsa replacement rejected

Aston Villa have had an £18million, plus £2m in add-ons bid for Taylor Harwood-Bellis rejected by Southampton, talkSPORT understands.

Villa are looking to sign a new centre-back before the end of the summer transfer window on September 1 as Ezri Konsa is on course to leave.



2 Villa's first offer is some £10million below Southampton's valuation of the player Credit: Getty

Premier League champions Arsenal are understood to have verbally agreed a deal worth £50m to sign the 28-year-old.

Tosin Adarabioyo and Fikayo Tomori are among a list of centre-back targets for Villa.

Another option is Harwood-Bellis, although an initial offer has been rebuffed with Saints valuing him at £30m.



Harwood-Bellis is a graduate of the Manchester City academy before making a permanent move to Southampton in 2024.

He initially joined on loan for the 2023/24 season, with his move then made permanent for a £20m fee after promotion to the top flight.



Harwood-Bellis, who is engaged to and is set to have a child with Roy Keane's daughter Leah, has made 134 appearances in defence for the Saints and been captain on numerous occasions.

The 24-year-old is also an England international as he earned his sole cap and scored against the Republic of Ireland in November 2024.



Who have Villa sold this summer?

Villa have experienced a summer of big change, despite winning the Europa League at the end of last season.

Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers and Lucas Digne are among the key departures for Unai Emery's side.

Ollie Watkins has been linked with a sensational move to Saudi club Al Hilal, and Emi Martinez could still leave amid a failed transfer to Juventus.

2 Konsa looks to be heading to Arsenal after seven seasons at Villa Credit: Getty



Should the pair exit Villa Park along with Konsa, then only five of the starting XI that beat SC Freiburg in the Europa League will be left.

They would be Matty Cash, Pau Torres, Victor Lindelof, John McGinn and Emi Buendia.

However, Villa have been active in terms of incomings, with Swiss star Johan Manzambi joining in a £51.2m move from Freiburg.

Joao Gomes then joined from West Midlands rivals Wolves for £35m.

On Wednesday, Villa completed the signings of Matteo Ruggeri and Zion Zuzuki.



The former has arrived from Atletico Madrid, whilst the latter signed from Parma.

Sports.title: Brighton CEO refuses to comment Manchester United’s pursuit of Carlos Baleba
Sports.content:
Brighton chief executive Paul Barber has confirmed the world's biggest clubs have shown interest in Carlos Baleba.

However, he refused to comment when asked about Manchester United's pursuit of the midfielder.

3 United are in advanced talks with Brighton over a deal for Baleba Credit: Getty

talkSPORT revealed on Wednesday that the Red Devils are in advanced talks with Brighton to sign Baleba.

It comes after a bid worth an initial £60million plus £5million in add-ons was placed for the 22-year-old.

United are confident of reaching an agreement with the Seagulls before the transfer window closes.

Baleba has already agreed to the move with personal terms in place.

Brighton CEO on Baleba interest

Barber joined White and Jordan live on talkSPORT on Thursday ahead of Brighton's Conference League play-off against Tromso.

When asked by Jim White if Baleba is joining United, though, he refused to comment on the transfer.

Instead, he replied: "It’s not something that I can talk about right now.

"This time of year we’re always going to be subject to bids for our players, we’re always going to be interested in ones that are sensible and are going to make sense for us financially, economically.

"But we also have to balance that with making sure our squad is as strong as it can be to compete in competitions like the one we’re in.

"So nothing really to say on Carlos at the moment other than that he’s a hugely talented young midfielder who’s done really well for us and has attracted interest from some of the biggest clubs in the world now for a couple of years."

3 Barber has revealed Baleba has attracted interest from some of the world's biggest clubs Credit: Alamy

Baleba has made 112 appearances for Brighton since joining the club from Lille in 2023.

The Cameroon international currently currently has just under two years remaining on his contract, although there is an option for a further 12 months.

United are also unfazed by an ankle injury suffered by Baleba in pre-season.

As a result of the setback, Baleba was absent from the Brighton squad for their trip to Norway to face Tromso.

Brighton stars in demand

The Seagulls' former Young Player of the Season is not the only one of their stars wanted by a Premier League rival.

Liverpool have seen a £50million bid for Yankuba Minteh rejected by Brighton.

3 Liverpool are interested in Minteh despite the fact he's nursing a leg injury Credit: Getty

talkSPORT previously revealed the Reds' interest in the winger back in June.

Minteh is currently sidelined until October with a leg injury suffered in a friendly against Roma earlier this month.

Following their eighth place finish last season, Brighton have already lost two key men this summer.

Defender Jan Paul van Hecke has moved to Tottenham Hotspur, whilst Chelsea swooped to complete a cut-price deal for Danny Welbeck.

Sports.title: Brazilian sources expecting imminent Endrick bid from Premier League giants
Sports.content:
Liverpool are poised to make a move for Real Madrid starlet Endrick, according to sources in Brazil.

South American football expert Tim Vickery told talkSPORT a substantial bid from the Reds for the 20-year-old striker is being rumoured.

3 Endrick featured for Brazil at this summer's World Cup Credit: Getty

Is an Endrick exit on the cards?

Endrick joined Real Madrid from Brazilian club Palmeiras in 2024 after a £51m deal was initially agreed in 2022, but he saw his opportunities limited last term and he ended up spending the second half of the season on loan at Lyon.

So, could he be on his way to the Premier League before the end of the transfer window?

Vickery said on Hawksbee and Jacobs: "Well, it's interesting that we've just been hearing about the victory of the lost king – probably everyone paying tribute to Kevin Keegan this weekend at Liverpool, and the loss of Mo Salah.

"Is Endrick going to be an attempt at the found king? Well, we shall see. I have my doubts.

"Not least because – and this is getting a lot of traction in Brazil at the moment...– Liverpool are apparently preparing an offer – big-money offer – but the fee that's being reported that Liverpool want to offer is less than Real Madrid for him a couple of years ago.

"Now, he hasn't been a failure at all, and the problem with Real Madrid is he went to a club that didn't need him – but his numbers even with Real Madrid aren't bad.

"And he did very well on loan with Lyon, so there's no way that he can be worth less than he was as an 18-year-old when Real Madrid bought him. So, that is, I think, problem number one.

"How high are Liverpool prepared to go? And would Real Madrid want to sell him to a competitor in the Champions League?"

Endrick's surprising idol

Vickery also pondered whether Endrick's admission of idolising a Manchester United icon would be well-received by Liverpool fans.

He continued: "One possible problem is, you know who one of his idols is? This is going to shock you; oh, I'm looking forward to this.

3 Endrick has scored seven goals for Real Madrid so far Credit: Getty

"Endrick, 20 years of age, one of his idols is... Ta-da! Bobby Charlton. Yes, yes, Bobby Charlton.

"You remember he scored a goal for Brazil. He scored the winner against England at Wembley just over two years ago...and he was saying, talking to Brazilian media afterwards, 'I'm delighted to have scored a goal in the place where, the very stadium where Bobby Charlton [starred for England and Man United].

"Is that going to go down well with the Kop and the Annie [Anfield] Road faithful?"

Vickery also highlighted Endrick's need to play in a front two, a system new Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola hasn't tended to deploy.

"I don't know," he went on. "He is a wonderfully talented player – really, really good player – but he does suffer, I think, a little bit from a question which I think affects a lot of players in his position – which is what exactly is his position?

"Can we go back to Kevin Keegan – [John] Toshack and Keegan? You know where you stood for the old 4-4-2 – big man in, a little man in; the little man is a second striker.

3 Endrick scored his first Brazil goal against England at Wembley aged 17 Credit: Getty

"I think ideally, he's probably that second striker, but a lot of these new-fangled modern-day formations, it's quite hard for that old second striker in a 4-4-2 to kind of define himself."

Liverpool look ahead to big kick-off

Liverpool have so far only made two signings as they prepare for the start of the Iraola era, bringing in centre-back Jeremy Jacquet in a deal that was arranged in January as well as winger Victor Munoz.

However, the Reds continue to be linked with a huge deal for Paris Saint-Germain and France star Bradley Barcola.

talkSPORT also understands they recently had an offer to sign Brighton winger Yankubah Minteh rejected.

Liverpool kick off the new Premier League campaign away to Newcastle on Sunday.

Sports.title: Liverpool have £50m bid for injured Premier League winger rejected
Sports.content:
Liverpool have seen a £50million offer for Brighton and Hove Albion winger Yankuba Minteh turned down, talkSPORT understands.

The approach from the Reds was immediately rebuffed by the Seagulls, and Liverpool are now contemplating a second bid for the currently injured forward.

2 Minteh has established himself as a dangerous winger Credit: Getty

Liverpool are looking to add some more wingers before the end of the transfer window.

Should they acquire Minteh before the September 1 deadline, he wouldn't be immediately available for them as he's currently nursing a leg injury, which could keep him out for up to three months.

The Reds have signed Victor Munoz, but are yet to replace Mohamed Salah on the right.

They've been linked with Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola, although the France international's preferred position is on the left wing.

As well as Minteh, Ibrahim Mbaye is also on Liverpool's list.

The 18-year-old Senegalese international is likely to see his game time become very limited in France.

This is because PSG have signed Maghnes Akliouche, Mika Godts and Ferran Torres.

Minteh's Premier League statistics

Minteh was bought by Brighton from Newcastle United without the winger making an appearance in black and white.

He was sold in the summer of 2024 to the Seagulls following a loan with Feyenoord.

In his first year, the Gambian international scored six goals and set up a further four.

Last year, the 22-year-old added three more goals and four further assists.

Not outstanding statistics in any way, but the winger is a constant ball of energy, always on the move and always looking to create and get shots off.

However, his injury could prove to be a problem.

The forward limped off during Brighton's pre-season friendly against Roma and has now been ruled out until potentially November.

2 Iraola is hoping for some attacking additions before the close of the transfer window Credit: Getty

More needed

Andoni Iraola has only seen three first-team signings arrive this summer.

And Reds legend Phil Thompson believes that the Liverpool board need to be very busy in the remainder of the window.

Speaking on Footy Accumulator's No Tippy Tappy Football podcast, he said: "Defensively, we do need more. It is a particular area if Jacquet isn't fully ready, who is going to be there? It's a difficult one. We still need recruitment.

"I think we probably need four, maybe five players in total in different positions. Defensively, certainly, a midfield player, a wide player; you need two quality players for every position. There's work to be done."

What have they done so far?

As of now, Liverpool have signed two centre-backs.

Jeremy Jacquet has come in from Rennes to replace Ibrahima Konate.

Julian Araujo has joined from Barcelona on loan with an option to buy to provide cover.

And Munoz was picked up from Osasuna after the Reds activated his release clause.

They start their Premier League campaign off against Newcastle United at St James' Park on Sunday.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta reveals Myles Lewis-Skelly’s Arsenal future has been decided
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has emphatically declared that Myles Lewis-Skelly will remain at Arsenal beyond the summer.

It was reported last week how the versatile Hale End graduate had been offered to Chelsea and Manchester United.

3 Lewis-Skelly starred in his last Arsenal outing to help them win the Community Shield Credit: Getty

Both clubs had previously been made aware of Lewis-Skelly's potential availability, with United showing interest in a move.

The 19-year-old's role in the squad this season had been questioned following the £75million arrival of Bruno Guimaraes.

Arteta didn't pour cold water on the exit rumours as he stated it is a 'good sign' that his players are linked with moves to other clubs.

Gunners supporters are desperate for the teenager to not be sold, with the England international establishing himself as a firm fan favourite.

Even former Newcastle and Crystal Palace boss Alan Pardew urged the Premier League champions to not sell the youngster - insisting it would be 'unforgivable'.

Lewis-Skelly once again showcased his supreme talent in his recent outing for Arsenal - just as he had done in the latter stages of the 2025/26 season.

Starting in Sunday's Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Lewis-Skelly expertly created Riccardo Calafiori's opener inside 25 seconds.

What has Mikel Arteta said about Myles Lewis-Skelly's Arsenal future?

Speaking ahead of Friday's Premier League opener at home to newly-promoted Coventry - live on talkSPORT - Arteta was asked in his press conference as to whether Lewis-Skelly will remain at the club.

To which he simply stated: "100 per cent."

Arteta was then pressed on whether Arsenal may have to follow suit like many of their top-flight rivals in recent years and sell their academy graduates.

3 Lewis-Skelly started just five Premier League games term from his 25 outings Credit: Getty

Like Lewis-Skelly, Ethan Nwaneri has been tipped to leave north London on a possible loan spell away following his stint at Marseille.

He was left out of the matchday squad for the Community Shield, with it expected he will be shipped out before the window slams shut.

Commenting on Arsenal's academy graduates, Arteta remarked: "The players that have been raised in our system, and they feel generally that love and that connection with the club, bring something else, there's no question about that.

"We need to look after them in a really special way because they bring value that is very difficult to find.

That's why, when we can, we want to protect those assets as much as possible, develop them and make them extremely important for the club."

And Arteta was also pressed on the difficulty of selling cult heroes, with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus believed to be up for sale.

3 Brazilian duo Martinelli and Jesus could be sold before the window closes Credit: Getty

To which the Spaniard remarked: "It's a really, really tough moment. We need to face that reality.

"But I think you need to face it with a real honesty and transparency because when you are on the other side, that's exactly what you need.

"You might not like what you've been told, but if it's truthful, if it's the reality, if it's honest and it's going to help you to make better decisions and have more clarity for the next steps in your career, you have to do that.

"These are always very difficult conversations, but they need to be done.

"It's like when a player doesn't feel that he belongs or he's important. He wants to have a different chapter. I think that communication has to exist and it has to be both ways.

"We all know that at the end, everything has a start and has an end.

"When it comes to the end, I think our duty, our responsibility is to do it in the best possible way, maintaining the respect and admiration for the player and the relationship, but understanding that at the end, we need to make football decisions."

Sports.title: Man United boss Michael Carrick says it is 'ridiculous' to suggest they have an easy start against Hull and Ipswich - and plays down talk of a Premier League title challenge
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick says it’s ‘ridiculous’ to suggest Manchester United have been handed an easy start to the season – and admits it’s asking a lot for his team to be considered title challengers.

United kick off the campaign at Hull City on Saturday lunchtime followed by a first home game against another of the newly-promoted teams, Ipswich Town, at Old Trafford the following week.

But Carrick has rejected claims that United have been given an easy ride, saying: ‘There are no favourable starts. It’s an easy thing to throw out there but pretty ridiculous.

‘It’s a tough start against both teams, but we’re not getting past Saturday. A newly-promoted team away from home will be a tough game.

‘That is the beauty of the new season. For teams coming up into the league, there tend to be quite a few changes. That is the challenge playing against them, we are fully aware of that. Mentally and physically we have done a lot of work. We are fully aware of what’s at stake and what’s coming at us.’

On United’s chances of delivering a first Premier League title since 2013 while coping with the demands of a Champions League return, Carrick added: ‘It’s going to be a jump. It doesn’t matter whether I say whether we can or can’t – and I would never say we can’t – it’s about what we can do, and what we are capable of doing as a group.

Carrick has rejected claims that United have been handed an easy start to the season, saying: ‘There are no favourable starts. It’s an easy thing to throw out there but pretty ridiculous'

United hope to add a third midfield signing of the summer after tabling a £65million offer for Brighton’s Carlos Baleba (right)

‘The run of form we had last season gives us confidence, but we know there is a whole new step to make as a group. We have the potential to achieve things and we have to believe we can do good things.’

United hope to add a third midfield signing of the summer after tabling a £65million offer for Brighton’s Carlos Baleba, having already spent £85m on Andrey Santos, of Chelsea, and Aston Villa’s Youri Tielemans. The club are also keen to strengthen at left-back.

Carrick was reluctant to say too much with another 11 days to go until the transfer window closes. ‘I just think we are looking to strengthen the squad, and we are working towards that,’ he said. ‘We’re certainly trying to make the most of the opportunities to finish the window stronger than we went into it, and I think we are in a good way to doing that so far.’

Marcus Rashford’s return from a loan spell at Barcelona has given United another option, and Carrick has been delighted with the England international’s attitude so far.

‘It has been pretty obvious that Marcus came back training with Kobbie (Mainoo) and Licha (Martinez) that he has come back fantastically well,’ added the United boss. ‘He looks strong, sharp and ready to play football. He can play through the middle, even though it’s not his No 1 position. We have forwards that give us that flexibility.’

Carrick had some positive injury news with Mason Mount close to fitness after missing the final two friendlies against Leeds and AC Milan with a foot injury. Benjamin Sesko, Matthijs De Ligt and new No 2 goalkeeper Karl Darlow, none of whom featured in pre-season, are also back in training.

‘Karl has trained this week, he is in good shape,’ said Carrick. ‘Mattha has been out for a long period of time, but he is training, and it’s great to have him back. He won’t be involved but he is in good shape and moving in a good direction, so that is a bonus for us. Ben is back training so that is another positive and we’re looking forward to having him back around the group and getting him some minutes.

‘We’re managing Mason a little bit, but he is very close. He’s touch and go for the weekend really and going into next week. Mason will be back very, very soon, if not immediately, so it's all good.’

Sports.title: Liverpool expected to make improved offer for Brighton for winger Yankuba Minteh after £50m bid was rejected - with club still locked in talks with PSG in deal for Bradley Barcola
Sports.content:
Liverpool are expected to make an improved offer for Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh after having a £50m bid rejected.

The Gambian is out until October after undergoing surgery on his right leg.

Liverpool reverted to the 22-year-old after considering Ibrahim Mbaye of Paris St Germain too expensive. They are continuing discussions for Bradley Barcola.

Daily Mail Sport reported upon Mohamed Salah’s departure that the Gambia international would feature on a list to bolster the wide forward position this summer.

While talks for Barcola are ongoing, they would preferably like two forwards with Ibrahim Mbaye, also of PSG, one sounded out last week.

Minteh is currently on the sidelines after suffering an injury in Brighton's pre-season win over Roma earlier this month.

Liverpool have approached Brighton over signing winger Yankuba Minteh this summer

Andoni Iraola's side are in the market to sign two forwards, with the club locked in talks over PSG's Bradley Barcola

Minteh has made 73 appearances for Brighton to date since joining from Newcastle in a £30m move in the summer of 2024. He has scored 10 goals and provided nine assists for the Seagulls.

Minteh predominantly plays on the right wing, but has also been used on the left by Fabian Hurzeler.

Meanwhile, Curtis Jones will have a medical at noon on Friday after Liverpool agreed to sell him to Inter Milan for £26.7m plus £4m in bonuses and a 10 percent sell-on.

The six-time England international, who joined Liverpool aged nine, has had his heart set on a move to Serie A for some time after failing to regularly establish himself as a starter at Anfield.

Liverpool are preparing for their first season under new manager Andoni Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot following the Dutchman's dismissal at the end of last season.

After spending over £450million on new signings including Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike last summer, the 2024-25 Premier League champions struggled to reach the same heights again under the Dutchman and only narrowly managed to qualify for the Champions League with a fifth-place finish last term.

Liverpool, who waved farewell to Mohamed Salah, Andrew Robertson and Ibrahima Konate at the start of the summer, have so far recruited centre-half Jeremy Jacquet from Stade Rennais and left winger Victor Munoz from Osasuna ahead of the new campaign.

Sports.title: RANGERS 1 JABLONEC 0: Ryan Naderi nets to nick a narrow lead but Ibrox men remain so unconvincing
Sports.content:
After taking a step forward with an emphatic victory over St Mirren in the Premier Sports Cup last weekend, this was a night when Rangers flirted with the idea of immediately taking two in the opposite direction.

In a UEFA Conference League play-off tie against Jablonec, Rangers made heavy weather of it - and then some.

A solitary goal from Ryan Naderi five minutes into the second half was enough to secure a one-goal lead as they head to the Czech Republic for next week's second leg.

But this is far from a done deal. Rangers remain far from convincing and no one can be sure that they will have group-stage football in Europe to look forward to for the season ahead.

The last time Rangers did not play in the group stage of a European competition was back in 2017 when they lost to Progres Niederkorn.

Derek McInnes and his players still have it all to do. Even against such limited opposition, Rangers were not impressive for the most part.

Ryan Naderi sees his effort hit the roof of the net to ensure Rangers take a first-leg lead

Rangers are denied as Jablonec defended stoutly at Ibrox

They were laborious in possession and largely devoid of creativity. They are still in the market for two new wingers and a new striker is possible.

It's not difficult to see why. The problem for McInnes is that he has already signed 11 new players. This is now very much his team and there looks to be precious little cohesion or attacking threat.

Rangers were clinging on towards the end after Cammy Devlin was shown a straight red card barely two minutes after coming off the bench.

It was a decision with which he could have no complaints, given it was high and it endangered his opponent.

If McInnes is to make a success of this job, it's difficult to overstate how important next week's return leg will be.

By hook or by crook, he and his players must come through it. If they were to be dumped out of Europe in two separate competitions by Jagiellonia Bialystok and Jablonec, it would be a major blot on his copybook.

Even this early in his tenure, he is fighting to convince some supporters he is the right man for the job. There is absolutely no style or identity to this team whatsoever.

Rangers were marginally improved in the second half but the overall paucity of the performance left the Ibrox crowd flat and underwhelmed, despite the slender victory.

When the Rangers team-sheet dropped prior to kick-off, more than a few eyebrows would have been raised at the fact Lawrence Shankland was once again on the bench.

McInnes had spoken pre-match about Shankland and insisted that he retained full confidence in the striker's ability to make a success of himself at Ibrox.

Yet, in a game of this magnitude, with European group-stage football on the line, there was something odd about the newly-appointed club captain not being in the starting XI.

Having deployed the team in a 4-3-3 shape in the 5-1 thrashing of St Mirren last weekend, McInnes clearly liked what he saw and stuck with it.

Naderi celebrates his goal, which could prove to be invaluable next week

Perhaps that's what went against Shankland, whose lack of mobility and ability to press makes him ill-suited to play the lone striker role in this system.

It was Ryan Naderi who got the nod up front, with the only change seeing Dan Neil coming in as captain to replace Nico Raskin in midfield.

For all they may not be the most glamorous of names to have graced Ibrox over the years, Jablonec arrived in confident mood on the back of six straight wins in all competitions.

The Czechs were quite content to sit in and frustrate Rangers in the early stages. In fairness, given the lack of creativity in the home side, it probably wasn't the most difficult of tasks.

Rangers lacked any guile or tempo in possession. Everything they did was one-paced and predictable, moving the ball from side to side, without any hint of penetration.

Manny Fernandez has been in poor form so far this season and it was notable just how nervous the crowd became when he was on the ball.

There looks to be a mistake in him at any moment. He picked up a booking after only 10 minutes and had to walk a tightrope for the remainder of the match.

As soon as Ben Godfrey is fit again, it is surely inevitable that he will come back into the team to partner Olwethu Makhanya and Fernandez will be dropped.

Rangers finally mustered a sight of goal on 25 minutes when some neat play in the penalty box saw Naderi lay the ball off to Vanja Dragojevic.

The Serbian midfielder had scored a screamer against St Mirren last weekend, but, on this occasion, his shot came back off the post and trickled along the goalline before the visitors were able to clear their lines.

Fernandez continued to be a bag of nerves. His body language was dreadful at times, moaning at others around him even though it was he who had made the mistake.

If there was a sense that the emphatic victory over St Mirren last weekend might imbue Rangers with a renewed sense of confidence, it simply did not materialise.

There were booed off at half-time. What made the performance so unimpressive was the fact that Jablonec were there for the taking.

Cammy Devlin saw red moments after coming on for Rangers as a second-half substitute

The Czechs could kindly be described as limited opposition. Even a semi-competent Rangers team would have been able to brush them aside with ease.

But this was another slog. The onus was on McInnes as manager to impart some kind of meaningful change heading into the second half.

With the crowd growing ever more restless, the breakthrough duly arrived within five minutes of the restart to ease the tension.

With what felt like his first forward pass all night, Neil clipped a ball to the back post, where Daisuke Yokota cushioned a header back across the face of goal.

With the goalkeeper out of position, Naderi, who had been largely anonymous, had the simple task of tapping home into the empty net.

The goal breathed new life into Rangers and it really ought to have been 2-0 just five minutes later when they cut the Czechs open down the right.

It was Naderi who whipped in a good cross to the far post for Djeidi Gassama. He met the ball first time on the volley and blazed it over when heading it may have been the better option.

Knowing that a one-goal lead would make for a nervy affair next week in the Czech Republic, Rangers were desperate to try and build on it if possible.

McInnes made a double change on 69 minutes, bringing on Devlin and Findlay Curtis as he tried to inject some fresh legs.

But it proved to be a disastrous cameo from Devlin, who, having only been on the pitch for a couple of minutes, went in late and high on Jablonec left-back Jiri Slama.

Romanian referee Marian Barbu appeared to miss the incident initially, but, after being referred to the monitor by the VAR, he showed Devlin a straight red card.

This was desperate for Rangers. It was now a case of backs to the wall and trying to cling on against a team who would be no more than mid-table in the Scottish Premiership.

They got the job done in the end, but it was a tough watch. Truth be told, they will settle for more of the same next week if the end result is a place in the group stage.

Sports.title: Man United progressing in Carlos Baleba talks with Brighton, Aston Villa table Ollie Watkins contract offer amid Saudi interest, and Man City see Adam Wharton enquiry rebuffed: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Man United progressing in Carlos Baleba talks with Brighton, Aston Villa table Ollie Watkins contract offer amid Saudi interest, and Man City see Adam Wharton enquiry rebuffed: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Man United progressing in Baleba talks

Manchester United are continuing discussions over a fee with Brighton for Carlos Baleba.

Brighton have rejected United’s £60million plus £5m for the midfielder but talks have been progressing to a compromise.

The 22-year-old Cameroon international is hoping the deal can be wrapped up over the weekend.

Meanwhile, United right-back Habeeb Ogunneye is scheduled to undergo a medical with Arsenal ahead of his move there.

The deal is understood to be a free transfer with 40percent sell-on clause.

The 20-year-old is being signed to boost numbers with Arsenal’s U21s but also train with the first team.

Man United have had a £65m offer for Carlos Baleba rejected but talks are progressing with Brighton

Clubs circle for Jackson

Atletico Madrid have enquired about a loan deal for Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson.

Atletico director Mateu Alemany was understood to have travelled to London on Thursday for talks.

Jackson also has interest from Aston Villa, Napoli and Saudi Arabia.

Meanwhile Chelsea forward Deivid Washington is a target for Marseilla, Strasbourg and Sevilla.

Blues defender Axel Disasi is continuing to discuss a loan move to Crystal Palace while Benoit Badiashile is joining Napoli. Leeds United are interested in striker Liam Delap as are Everton.

Spurs talk numbers

Tottenham are working on figures with City for Savinho and forward Omar Marmoush. The deal for Savinho could be worth up to £84m.

City have also asked about Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton as they work through a list of targets.

Leeds swoop for goalkeeper Zetterer

Leeds United are closing on a deal for Eintracht Frankfurt goalkeeper Michael Zetterer to come in as James Trafford's deputy.

The clubs are finalising agreement for the 31-year-old, but Frankfurt need to find a new goalkeeper to replace Zetterer first.

Leeds are waiting for Lucas Perri to fully recover from a minor injury before he completes his delayed loan move to Torino.

Zetterer, 31, is a former Germany U21 international.

Southampton reject Villa approach for Harwood-Bellis

Aston Villa have been rebuffed in an enquiry for Southampton defender Taylor Harwood-Bellis.

Villa are willing to offer around £17.5m for the 24-year-old but Saints had already rejected a similar offer from Benfica.

Talks are ongoing as Villa assess options such as Tosin Adarabioyo at Chelsea and Fikayo Tomori of AC Milan to fill the void left by Ezri Konsa's move to Arsenal.

Villa have been rebuffed in an enquiry for Southampton defender Taylor Harwood-Bellis

City keep watching brief on Wharton

Manchester City maintain an interest in Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton.

The Selhurst Park club are reluctant to lose the 22-year-old this summer but have been making significant enquiries for midfielders in recent weeks.

City are exploring several options including Manu Kone at Roma while they are advancing in talks to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille and are assessing the cost of a bid for Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez.

'We did it [sold big players in the past], and now is not the moment to do that,' said Palace boss Pierre Sage on Thursday.

'He is able to play in another club, a big club. Here, or anywhere in Europe, but one year with us, in a new dynamic, will be good for him. And we need him - that is why I think he will stay with us.'

Wharton has been a significant Premier League performer in recent seasons and excelled in the Europa League Conference final but analysts at some top level would-be suitors have indicated his running statistics do not reflect someone who can fit into a high-pressing style.

He continues to show on the pitch, however, an ability to find the right pass and shield his defence.

City have also made contact with Palmeiras for winger Allan Elias as they seek a replacement for Savinho.

Allan, 22, wants to join City but his club are reluctant to sell now with their season running to December. Talks are ongoing over a £35million fee.

SIMON JONES AND BOBBY MANZI

Manchester City have seen an enquiry for Adam Wharton rebuffed by Crystal Palace

Jones set for Inter medical

Inter Milan expect Curtis Jones to arrive later today ahead of a £30.7million move from Liverpool. The Italian side have scheduled Jones' medical for midday on Friday.

Inter bid £26.7m plus £4m in add-ons with a 10 per cent sell-on clause, offering a similar structure to the deal used to sign Djed Spence from Tottenham.

Curtis Jones is set to sign a five-year deal with Inter

Jones, 25, will sign a five-year deal with the Serie A champions.

Meanwhile, Liverpool centre back Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, is in talks to join Levante on loan. Ndukwe does not qualify for a work permit in England so must be loaned out. Liverpool remain in talks over PSG winger Bradley Barcola.

Sheffield Wednesday are to confirm the signing of Liverpool's Northern Ireland international winger Kieran Morrison on a season-long loan.

Hammers close on Mukasa

West Ham are close to an agreement to sign highly-rated Manchester City forward Divine Mukasa on loan for the season.

There is no buy option for the 18-year-old who spent the second half of last season on loan at Leicester City

City step up hunt for Savinho replacement

Manchester City have asked about Palmeiras winger Allan Elias as they consider replacements for Savinho.

Allan is 22 but has not been capped by Brazil. Quick and skilful, he is not a goalscorer but has earned a reputation as a worker, willing to press.

Newcastle United and Aston Villa have also scouted him in recent months.

City are evaluating several options with Tottenham working on the deal to sign Savinho and forward Omar Marmoush.

Bayern reach Palhinha agreement

Bayern Munich have reached a full agreement with Benfica over the £17million sale of Joao Palhinha.

The 31-year-old midfielder had been a target for Aston Villa and Newcastle United but will now reunite with his former Fulham boss Marco Silva at Benfica.

Villa were only willing to take him on an initial loan which Bayern refused.

Villa table new contract offer to Watkins

Aston Villa have made a new contract offer to striker Ollie Watkins.

The 30-year-old is open to a move to Al Hilal who had a £38.5m offer rejected on Tuesday but are preparing a fourth offer for the England international.

Watkins has scored consistently throughout his Villa career and his goals would be difficult to replace.

Villa have maintained contacts over Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson who also has interest from Napoli but he is valued around £65m.

Aston Villa have put forward a new contract offer to striker Ollie Watkins

Wrexham make move for ex-United star

Wrexham are continuing discussions with free agent Axel Tuanzebe.

The 28-year-old Congo international left Burnley at the end of last season and has had interest from clubs but is interested in Wrexham's ambitious project.

Wrexham are in talks to sign former Manchester United defender Axel Tuanzebe

Palace return for Auxerre target

Crystal Palace have rekindled interest in Auxerre midfielder Kevin Danois.

The 22-year-old was discussed as an option in January and Palace have made further enquiries.

The France U21 international is an attacking player who can also play out wide and was on Newcastle United's list earlier in the year.

Hull advance in talks for Betis star Garcia

Hull City owner Acun Ilicali has confirmed they are making progress on their bid to sign Real Betis winger Pablo Garcia and remain in talks for Deportivo La Coruna winger Yeremay Hernandez.

'I think probably, if nothing unknown happens, we will see him in a black and gold shirt. It has to be finalised, but I would say 90 percent of this deal is done. We are talking about the last details,' said Ilicali.

Pictures of Hernandez in Hull have been posted on social media, and Ilicali told BBC Humberside: 'We have to get the club side done and Yeremay also wants to come but it is a very vital, critical decision for himself. This deal is a very hard deal but we are somewhere where it looks positive.

'He is a young boy and it would change his life completely so he wanted to see where he would come. We will see in three, four days if this deal will be done or not. If it happens it will be a record for sure.'

Race on for Black Cats Ta Bi

West Ham and Burnley have expressed interest in Sunderland winger Jocelin Ta Bi.

The 21-year-old only joined Sunderland from Maccabi Netanya in January and signed a four and a half year contract.

He made one appearance in the FA Cup against Oxford United and then started against Fulham in the Premier League.

As it stands, the Championship clubs have expressed interest but talks have not gone further.

Wolves 'keeper Dan Bentley has joined Coventry City on a free as back up to Carl Rushworth.

Charlton are signing Wrexham goalkeeper Arthur Okonkwo on a season loan.

Stoke are keen on Manu Duah from San Diego.
