Sports.title: HEARTS 2 RAPID VIENNA 2: Wilson's wonder strike has Tynecastle in raptures but Gorgie men are pegged back for draw
Sports.content:
HEARTS 2 RAPID VIENNA 2: Wilson's wonder strike has Tynecastle in raptures but Gorgie men are pegged back for draw

Hearts’ hopes of avoiding the ignominy of being knocked out of three different European competitions in the space of six weeks at the start of the season are in the balance following a dramatic night in Gorgie.

After trailing to Serge-Philippe Raux-Yao’s goal at the interval, a stirring second half display looked like it might be enough to take a lead to Vienna for the second leg of their Conference League play-off round tie.

Josh McPake’s equaliser and a sensational strike from James Wilson - a goal which will live long in Hearts folklore - put Wouter Vrancken’s side in front and had Tynecastle rocking.

Hearts striker James Wilson celebrates after scoring a 30-yard screamer

Austrian Bundesliga leaders Rapid reinstated themselves as firm favourites to reach the league phase of the competition, however, when sub Nikolaus Wurmbrand restored parity in the closing stages.

Hearts now have it all to do in the second leg next Wednesday if they are to avoid that unwanted hat-trick after already losing in the qualifying rounds of the Champions League and Europa League.

Having already conceded 13 times over the course of those ties against Sturm Graz and Benfica, trying to tighten up defensively was an obvious priority for Hearts.

That was never going to be easy against a free-wheeling Rapid outfit who arrived in Edinburgh having racked up 29 goals in winning all eight of their competitive matches so far this season.

It didn’t take them long to showcase their attacking prowess with only an exceptional piece of goalkeeping from Beau Reus preventing Hearts from falling behind after just nine minutes.

Rapid weaved their way into the home penalty area with pace and precision to leave Matthias Seidl one-on-one with the Hearts keeper. The Rapid captain struck his shot cleanly enough but was denied by a superb save from Reus.

The big Dutchman was called into action again three minutes later and once again was up to the task. Jannes Horn found space on the left to clip in a cross which Bendeguz Bolla met with a crisp header on the edge of the six yard box.

James Wilson lets fly from distance to put Hearts 2-1 up against Rapid Vienna

Rapid’s Hungarian defender was already in the throes of celebrating what looked like a certain goal when Reus threw himself to his left and somehow clawed the ball away to safety.

Claudio Braga did his best to ease the early anxiety and lift the mood of the Hearts support. Regardless of persistent speculation he will be sold by Hearts before the summer transfer window closes, there has been no drop-off in the work rate and commitment which made Braga Scotland’s Player of the Year last season.

The Portuguese forward got Hearts onto the front foot for a spell with his powerful running and clever positional play. Unfortunately, it wasn’t matched by central striker Pierre Landry Kabore whose tendency to dwell just too long in possession earned him the groans and moans of the home fans.

Serge-Philippe Raux-Yao scores the opening goal for Rapid Vienna

At the other end of the pitch, Hearts continued to invite their own problems. Rapid had clearly identified Jordi Altena as a potential weak link and the Hearts right-back did nothing to confound that assessment.

Altena, not for the first time, was careless in possession when he played a blind pass across the face of his own defensive third in the 28th minute. It went straight to Tonni Adamsen but, fortunately for Hearts, the Danish striker couldn’t take advantage as his tame shot was comfortably held by Reus.

Despite that warning shot, Altena failed to learn his lesson and it proved damaging for Hearts as they fell behind two minutes later.

Altena coughed up possession needlessly once more, forcing team-mate Oisin McEntee to mop up after him at the expense of a corner. Bolla took it from the left, picking out Seidl on the edge of the box.

He flicked it on to Raux-Yao who had all the time and space he could wish for to head past Reus from close range. A lengthy VAR check suggested there might be a reprieve for Hearts but the big defender had indeed stayed just onside.

The goal inevitably deflated the mood inside Tynecastle but Hearts rallied towards the end of the first half to offer some indication they were capable of finding a way back into the tie.

McPake cut in from the left and drilled in a low shot which Rapid goalkeeper Niklas Hedl did well to clutch at his right hand post.

Braga and Tom Renaud also tried their luck from distance, the former’s effort flying narrowly wide before the latter forced another save from Hedl.

That promise of better things to come was fulfilled as Hearts made a vibrant start to the second half, cranking up a spell of pressure which saw them stun Rapid and overturn the interval deficit.

Hearts winger Josh McPake scores to make it 1-1 at Tynecastle

Braga continued to provide the spark and was unlucky to see a shot deflected just wide of Hedl’s right hand post.

Kabore finally followed his lead and made a worthy contribution to Hearts’ 56th minute equaliser with a clever reverse pass to set McPake free on the left of Rapid’s penalty area. The former St Johnstone winger steadied himself and curled in a shot which took a wicked deflection off Raux-Yao to leave Hedl helpless as the ball flew into the top of his net.

It was Kabore’s last involvement before he was replaced by Wilson. As Hearts looked to make the most of the momentum now with them, Jamie McCart sent a header agonisingly wide of Hedl’s left hand post from a Blair Spittal corner.

The home team’s second goal was on the way, however, and was worth waiting for. It’s one which will be fondly recalled in Gorgie for a long time to come.

There appeared to be little danger to Rapid when Wilson gathered the ball 30 yards out after a long clearance from Reus. Spotting Hedl off his line, however, the striker smashed a magnificent shot over him and into the top left hand corner of the net.

Sadly for Wilson and Hearts, it wasn’t the winner it richly deserved to be. Rapid regained control in the final 20 minutes and deserved to make it 2-2 when Wurmbrand’s shot was deflected beyond Reus after Hearts passed up several chances to clear a corner.

Sports.title: TNT Sport bosses bemused by Joe Cole after pundit bizarrely claimed Hull City have arrived in the Premier League 'through the back door' and he snubbed call to cover opening game - as Tigers owner hits back
Sports.content:
TNT Sport bosses bemused by Joe Cole after pundit bizarrely claimed Hull City have arrived in the Premier League 'through the back door' and he snubbed call to cover opening game - as Tigers owner hits back

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Joe Cole has sparked a furious response from Hull City fans after claiming the Tigers are already relegated - and saying he put his phone on ‘do not disturb’ to ensure he would not have to be a pundit for TNT Sports at their season opener against Manchester United tomorrow night.

The former Chelsea and England man has triggered outrage in East Yorkshire thanks to comments he made with former West Ham team-mate Carlton Cole on a podcast.

When asked who would be going down this season, Cole said ‘Hull are gone, man’ before claiming that they had arrived in the Premier League ‘through the back door’.

He then added that he had ‘a confession to make’, saying he had been contacted by TNT Sports who ‘tried to slip in Hull on the first day of the season’. ‘I put my phone on Do Not Disturb,’ he said.

Hull City are GOING DOWN! 🗣️🐯



The lads don’t rate Hull’s chances this season 🥺



Watch in full 👉 https://t.co/PuonqV3D90#TheDressingRoom #PremierLeague #PL pic.twitter.com/B1xa8RV4nI — The Dressing Room Podcast (@dressingroomaa) August 19, 2026

Joe Cole has risked the wrath of Hull City fans with comments made on his podcast

Daily Mail Sport understands the comments have left bosses at TNT Sports bemused, with insiders saying Cole was not down to cover the opener at the MKM Stadium, and never had been.

Regardless, it has stoked plenty of emotion in Hull. Sources have disclosed that players and staff are well aware of what was said and intend to use it as motivation for what would appear to be a tough mission ahead.

Fans have taken to social media to highlight what they see as a ‘condescending’ and ‘disrespectful’ attitude, with some even claiming the newly-promoted club, who won the Championship play-off final, should ban Cole from its stadium.

Hull owner Acun Ilicali responded to the comments from both Coles on social media, writing: 'It is disappointing to see my beautiful city criticised by people who should know better.

'As a club we are used to being underestimated and we enjoy it, and we enjoyed it more when were promoted last season.

'The true beauty of a place is in its people, and that’s why, for me, Hull is one of the most beautiful places in the world.

'For me, seeing two ex-players making fun of a deservedly promoted club, is more laughable than the things they were laughing at.'

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso refuses to rule out Enzo Fernandez exit with Chelsea set to demand MORE than £120m asking price for star man after Man City missed transfer deadline
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso refused to guarantee that Enzo Fernandez will be staying this summer – but believes he can overcome the Chelsea boo-boys if he does not depart for Manchester City.

Fernandez received a mixed reaction in their final friendly at Stamford Bridge before the Premier League begins. The 25-year-old Argentinian replaced Reece James against Real Sociedad – and took the captain’s armband – as he was both jeered and cheered by his own fans.

Speaking on the eve of the 2026-27 season starting, and with Chelsea away at Fulham on Monday, Alonso said: 'It's not unusual. It can happen. We support him. We have a great player with Enzo, a top player, so important. I am happy that when I see him training, you see that he has a competitive mentality. We work with him every day very well.’

Alonso also hinted Fernandez would remain his vice-captain under James. Asked if he can see Chelsea’s supporters getting behind the midfielder, Alonso added: ‘I’m sure it will happen because this is a normal situation in football. Once we start the competition, we need the support.

‘We need the full commitment of all the team and of all the supporters when they come to Stamford Bridge. That we are pushing in the same direction.’

Xabi Alonso has refused to be drawn on whether Enzo Fernandez will be a Chelsea player when the transfer window closes

City's interest in Fernandez has been no secret this summer, though the side managed by Enzo Maresca have yet to submit a formal offer for the Argentina international. Chelsea were previously asking for £120million, but the Blues say those terms expired with the deadline they set for bids last Friday. City could be quoted a higher asking price if they sought one now.

Alonso dodged answering any and all questions about whether Fernandez would be staying with Chelsea at his pre-Fulham press conference, choosing instead to highlight how well he is training.

‘Enzo is a Chelsea player,’ Alonso said when asked directly if Fernandez would still be with Chelsea beyond deadline day. ‘He's a top, top player. He's training really well since he started 10 days ago with the team, very integrated. We are happy with him and he's getting ready for Monday.

‘He's training really well. I see him with a good attitude. That's what we want. He’s a player, he’s training well, he’s preparing for Monday and that’s my concern at the moment.’

Fernandez was previously used as a No 10 at Chelsea, though Alonso did hint he sees him in a deeper role rather than competing with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers.

‘He can do both,’ Alonso said. ‘I think when he's with the ball, he has the qualities to link the short passes but the long ones as well. He's able to see short and the farther players and from there he can progress. But he’s played great as a No 10 as well.’

Sports.title: No ego, refreshingly candid and the polar opposite of Oliver Glasner: This is what I learned from Pierre Sage's brilliant first press conference as Crystal Palace boss - from his tactical 'three pillars' to transfer clues on Sarr, Wharton and more
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace's press suite has benefitted from a luxurious summer refurbishment. Not only have the plastic chairs better suited to a school classroom been replaced by rows of leather seating, there is also a new man in the hotseat.

Palace have erased any lasting memories of Oliver Glasner – who switched allegiances to their new rivals Nottingham Forest – changing the layout of the room, the screens and brutally ripping the photo of the Austrian celebrating the club's FA Cup win off the wall.

In his place sat Pierre Sage, the French coach who secured Champions League football at Lens last season and won the French Cup. An intelligent, dignified and sincere communicator.

Sage sat with the media for 40 minutes on Thursday, and the main takeaway was this: he could not be more different to his predecessor.

There are just two striking similarities between Sage and Glasner – they play the same formation and are fascinated by social science. Sage, after all, lectured on sports mentality for 10 years at Claude Bernard University in Lyon.

Even in his first Premier League press conference, the differences between Crystal Palace's new boss Pierre Sage (pictured) and his predecessor Oliver Glasner were evident

Glasner's dealings with the media were often spiky last season, as he complained whenever he didn't get his way

At the start of the year, Glasner's interactions with the press were spiky. He frequently played mind games with the club and its supporters, throwing his toys out of the pram – rightly or wrongly – whenever he did not get his own way. It was box office but draining.

Sage, on the other hand, was refreshing. There was no equivocating, just candid conversation. Despite admitting he is a reserved character, he sat down and exuded a genuine transparency.

'I’m quiet, shy, maybe,' Sage said. 'But when I speak and I’m hungry, they know.'

Perhaps that is because he is not a product of the football establishment. There was no professional playing career, he had nothing handed to him. Sage was an amateur footballer and coach with an aspiration shared by millions: elite football.

'Four or five years ago, my dream was to become a member of staff – not a manager – at a pro team... I did it,' Sage added. 'But I did it in a way I didn’t consider and I became a head coach. It works well. That’s why I told myself I needed a new dream, and two years ago that dream became coming to the Premier League. Now I am here. I have to build another dream.

'I’m a flag bearer of the amateur coach and for young coaches to give them hope to become a head coach of a good team, a professional team. You need to work every day. To have an opportunity, you have to be an opportunity yourself.

'I came from the bottom. Now I’m here, I just want to give my best. I have no pressure. For me, the pressure is giving the players the best session I can give every day. Sometimes there will be a gap between what we did in game and what we chose before the game. But our job is to make the gap as small as we can, improve the way we play and develop our game.'

'Two years ago my dream became coming to the Premier League,' said Sage. 'Now I am here. I have to build another dream'

Sage accepted it may take a while to place his imprint on the team, with staggered arrivals throughout pre-season because 13 Palace players were at the World Cup. But he will adopt Glasner's style of play to an extent and gradually integrate his ideas to ensure Palace get off to the best start possible.

That was not laying the groundwork for an excuse, though, just pragmatism. He still expects results from himself and his team from week one, starting at Everton on Saturday.

'We have to consider the late arrivals of the players and accept what the players are able to do collectively now,' Sage added. 'But we want to implement our principles because that will give us more options to win games.

'We will do that session after session, game after game. The most important thing is to play as a team, respect every moment of play and every moment of the game because we want to play as a unit.

'I always speak about three pillars. The first is about pressing, we want to recover the ball as soon as we can because we want to play with the ball and be efficient in build-up, creating good possession conditions in the opponents' half. At the end, we want to attack the depths (high areas) and put pressure, psychological pressure and space pressure on the opponents in games.

'We are able to do that in transition and by having the ball in possession. We want to be able to play in a lot of contexts to compete. We have a focus on set-pieces because they’re important to win games and make a difference in some moments.'

Could transfer exits rock the boat?

As far as Sage is concerned, Adam Wharton, Ismaila Sarr and Daniel Munoz will all remain at Palace beyond the closure of the summer transfer window.

Manchester City enquired for Wharton but were knocked back, with Palace maintaining he is not for sale. In any case, their current valuation of the midfielder exceeds £100million.

Meanwhile, Galatasaray had a bid north of £30million turned down for Sarr this week. Palace value the Senegal international significantly above his market value.

Everton have assessed Munoz, although they are currently exploring moves for other targets at right back.

Besides Romain Esse, who Sage explicitly stated was not a part of his plans, the Palace boss is looking to build his squad, not dismantle it further. Daily Mail Sport understands Palace want to add two centre backs and a midfielder before the window closes.

Manchester City have shown interest in Palace midfielder Adam Wharton but the club are adamant he's not for sale

'We will, we will,' Sage responded when asked if Palace will keep Sarr. 'He’s a really important player for the club and for us. He played in the World Cup with Senegal and joined the group three weeks ago. He will be able to play this weekend.'

'We did it (sold players) and now it’s not the moment to do that,' he said of Wharton's future. 'He is able to play in another club, a big club, here or anywhere in Europe. But one year with us and a new dynamic will be good for him. We need him and that’s why he will stay with us. I hope he continues his improvement.'

As for Munoz, Sage was blunt: 'I hear the noise but he is happy to be with us and we are happy he is here.'

He applied the pressure on the recruitment team, too, urging them to sign a centre back with Premier League experience. Palace are in talks to loan Axel Disasi from Chelsea.

Palace will start the Premier League season without a central centre back after Maxence Lacroix joined Chelsea. They are also yet to secure a replacement for Marc Guehi, who left the club seven months ago.

Glasner would have used that as a stick to beat the board with. It became his transfer window trademark, lambasting the board for sluggish business.

Sage, instead, made his point – but with humility. Whether a level-headed approach will work with Palace chairman Steve Parish remains to be seen; Glasner's rants often sprang him into action.

Deep down, Sage will be annoyed he is starting the season with an incomplete backline but publicly he toed the party line and said he would rather wait for the right option. The sign of a leader without ego.

Does Matheus Franca have a future at Palace?

It has been a tough three years for Matheus Franca since arriving at Palace. He signed for £17million as a promising teenager from Brazil and took Wilfried Zaha's number 11 shirt.

The expectations were high for a player most knew nothing about and he subsequently faltered at every opportunity. He has played just 14 league games for Palace, spending most of the time injured or out of favour.

Last season, he went back to Brazil to join Vasco da Gama on loan. He did not set the world alight there either.

But there has been a glimpse of the player Palace had such high hopes for in pre-season, with Franca scoring four times and looking comfortable playing as a No9 rather than his usual position out wide.

Matheus Franca has had a difficult sime since moving to Palace from Brazil as a teenager, but his performances in pre-season have been encouraging

New manager Sage believes all is not lost on Franca: 'He had a good pre-season with four goals. It was difficult for him as he began here, that’s why he went on loan to Brazil last year.

'He has to adapt to European football because it’s really different to South American football. He’s shown really good things and we will see what we will do with him. We have to build the best context for him to improve because he’s young but he has talent.'

Where does Cheick Doucoure fit in?

Cheick Doucoure has not played a competitive game in 18 months after rupturing his ACL just a year after recovering from an achilles injury. The midfielder, once touted with a £70million move to Liverpool, has had multiple years shaved off his career.

Yet after a stable pre-season, he is back at Palace's disposal and ready to play in the Premier League. It will take time before he is anywhere near his best. There is a chance he will never be the same player he was. Nevertheless, Sage is excited to work with an 'incredible player'.

'He’s able to start,' said Sage. 'He didn’t play much during the last two seasons so we have to consider him within this situation. He needs time to come back and we will take our time to let him in a good context, particularly on the psychological side.

'When you play, you have to be confident, understand this moment is only a step and in a few moments you will be the player you were two years ago. That’s why we will take our time with him.

'He understands that. He walks a lot around the session but he’s really happy to be on the pitch and we are happy to see him on the pitch because he’s an incredible player.'

Sports.title: Man Utd's Carlos Baleba deal shows they've learnt from Frenkie de Jong mistake
Sports.content:
Man Utd's Carlos Baleba deal shows they've learnt from Frenkie de Jong mistake

Manchester United are closing in on signing Brighton's Carlos Baleba in another fast-moving piece of transfer business, unlike their days of chasing Frenkie de Jong to no avail

View 2 Images Manchester United tried to get Frenkie de Jong in 2022 (Image: Catherine Ivill/Getty Images)

No galactico signings, no tedious sagas. Is this really a Manchester United transfer window?

‌



There was plenty of noise going into the summer about United's midfield rebuild, yet they've gone about their business relatively quietly. Andrey Santos' move from Chelsea came out of the blue, while the decision to trigger Youri Tielemans' £35million release clause made for another smooth transaction.

‌



Now Carlos Baleba is in line to become United's next rapid-fire signing. Prior to Wednesday's news that the Red Devils had submitted a £65m bid, reports suggested that the Brighton midfielder was no longer a priority, with the likes of Sander Berge, Manu Kone and Aurelien Tchouameni said to be preferred.

‌



Instead, they've sprung a surprise and quickly made progress on Baleba. It's a stark contrast to how United operated in the summer of 2022 when their public pursuit of Frenkie de Jong highlighted their lacklustre transfer strategy and ended in predictable failure.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



United went about their move for De Jong in quite literal broad daylight. CEO Richard Arnold and sporting director John Murtagh - each of them no longer at the club - were spotted in Barcelona in mid-July 2022 before reaching an agreement in principle for De Jong.

That was only club-to-club, however, and the Dutchman's reluctance to join the Red Devils proved a stumbling block. BBC Sport report that even though United's recruitment staff had been told that signing De Jong was impossible, Erik ten Hag was certain it could be done, dragging out the saga for the best part of two months.

De Jong's stance never changed and after two losses in Ten Hag's first two games, United were forced to pivot. They coughed up £70m to sign a 30-year-old Casemiro and handed him a bumper four-year contract.

‌



It feels apt that in the summer Casemiro departed, the new Old Trafford hierarchy are showing that they've learned from their predecessors' mistakes. Fans have been frustrated by the lack of updates since signing Tielemans on July 14, but in reality United have worked hard to keep a low profile and maintain a stealthy approach.

Is Carlos Baleba a good signing for Manchester United? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Manchester United will have to raise their bid for Carlos Baleba (Image: Glyn KIRK/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



It should be noted that there's still work to do on Baleba, with United's offer of £60m plus £5m in add-ons not being sufficient. Nevertheless, expect the Cameroon international to be a United player by deadline day.

United did the groundwork on Baleba last summer when Brighton quoted them an eye-watering £100m off the back of his star-making season, so they'll have saved a good chunk of money by being patient. And could their latest move also serve as a blueprint for next year?

The Red Devils would also like to sign Lewis Hall, but given that Newcastle have already sold several key players this summer, it's an unlikely outcome. In 12 months' time, though, Hall will be a year closer to the expiry of his current contract and potentially more attainable.

Sports.title: York Ebor Festival tips: Friday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy
Sports.content:
1.50 Sky Bet Mile Handicap - EXCLUSIVE CODE has one big prize from a marquee summer meeting on his CV - and another may not be far away.

After fourth placings in a novice stakes at Newbury and a maiden at Goodwood - the latter on terrain with give in it - last summer, the three-year-old son of Blue Point returned from a 259-day abeyance to land a 25-runner maiden at the former track in April.

Archie Watson was then tempted to take aim at the Britannia Handicap over the straight mile at Royal Ascot, but a draw in stall three meant Exclusive Code’s challenge was over before it began.

Andrew Balding writes new ending to £1.5m summer blockbuster with unbeaten Item READ MORE :

In the circumstances, a 13th behind Moonfall - he came home third of the 15 horses racing towards the far side - was a decent effort and Exclusive Code went off a well-backed 2-1 favourite for the one-mile handicap for three-year-olds at Glorious Goodwood.

‌



James Doyle’s mount duly netted the money with a one-length beating of Zennor Storm and, with more to come, is the choice to stay ahead of the runner-up despite being on 4lb worse terms for the rematch.

Bearish , the progressive winner of his handicap debut at Ayr last time, is expected to go well, while Le Samourai and St Anton also make appeal.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 EXCLUSIVE CODE, 2 BEARISH, 3 ZENNOR STORM

View 7 Images Amiloc has been tipped by Newsboy

‌



2.25 Weatherbys Lonsdale Cup - AMILOC, at the centre of a calamity at Glorious Goodwood, should enjoy better luck today.

Unbeaten as a two-year-old in 2024, Postponed’s son continued his upward curve in the care of Ralph Beckett last season, coming home in front on the South Downs on his first two starts before tackling Group 2 company to land the King Edward VII Stakes at Royal Ascot.

Amiloc then moved up to the highest level and looked anything out of place in returning a four-length second to Al Riffa in the Irish St Leger over a mile and three-quarters at the Curragh and a staying-on fourth in the Breeders’ Cup Turf over two furlongs shorter at Del Mar.

My selection flopped when a well-backed 8-13 hotpot for the Group 2 Yorkshire Cup on the Knavesmire in May but his sixth to Giavellotto in the same-level Hardwicke Stakes back at Royal Ascot was much more like it.

‌



Amiloc attracted support for the Group 1 Goodwood Cup, his first attempt at two miles, 24 days ago but lurched to his left leaving the stalls and unshipped Hector Crouch, who makes way for Rossa Ryan here.

He therefore has to prove his staying power but shapes as if he will last the distance, and a bold show is on the cards. Caballo De Mar is feared most, ahead of Carmers and Mount Atlas.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 AMILOC, 2 CABALLO DE MAR, 3 MOUNT ATLAS

View 7 Images Michael Dods: trains Arapaho Gold (Image: PA)

‌



3.00 Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack Stakes - ARAPAHO GOLD is unbeaten - and fancied to stay that way.

Michael Dods’ illustrious training career has seen the Co Durham trainer lift numerous big prizes, including Group 1 victories with Mecca’s Angel and Mabs Cross. And Arapaho Gold could be bound for the top level, based on the evidence of his three outings so far.

There was clearly some confidence behind the son of Bayside Boy when he began his career in a five-furlong maiden at Thirsk at the beginning of May - Arapaho Gold went off at 7-2 in a field of eight and won easily, beating Kodiak Breeze by two and a half lengths.

An evident mistrust of the starting stalls needs monitoring - my selection was withdrawn from at Beverley four weeks later after rearing up in the structure - but all was well when Connor Beasley’s partner returned to Thirsk to justify odds of 2-9 over six furlongs in July.

‌



His three-and-three-quarter-length humbling of Mick’s The Boy led to a challenge for the Listed Rose Bowl Stakes at Newbury a further 16 days on and, despite being barged into by an opponent early on, Arapaho Gold kept his composure to make it 3-3, leading at the furlong marker to hold Nabati by a neck.

There is plenty more where that came from, with Adaay In Scarlett, and Marco Polo and Mussab the best candidates for the podium.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 ARAPAHO GOLD, 2 ADAAY IN SCARLETT, 3 MARCO POLO

View 7 Images American Affair: Newsboy's pick

‌



3.35 Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes - AMERICAN AFFAIR, back at the peak of his powers, earns the vote to double his Group 1 tally.

The Jim Goldie-trained speedster, having landed Doncaster’s Portland Handicap in September of the previous year, enjoyed an annus mirabilis in 2025.

American Affair started the campaign by beating Jm Jungle for the Scottish Sprint Cup Handicap at Musselburgh in April, had the same rival in second in a similar event over this afternoon’s course and distance the following month and then notched a first top-level triumph for both himself and his trainer with a neck call from Frost At Dawn in Royal Ascot’s King Charles III Stakes.

Plans to take in the Nunthorpe and the Breeders’ Cup were shelved when Washington DC’s son suffered a bone injury in a fetlock joint, and the road back in 2026 included defeats on his first four outings.

‌



But his connections’ patience received its reward as the six-year-old roared back to winning form in the Group 2 King George Stakes at Glorious Goodwood.

Leading at the halfway point of the five furlongs, American Affair charged home to beat Rumstar by half a length, with Time For Sandals (third), Asfoora (fourth), Jm Jungle (fifth), Partisan Hero (seventh), Night Raider (10th) and Azure Angel (15th) further back. There should be yet more to come and, proven on the track and on rain-softened terrain, American Affair ticks a lot of boxes.

Market leaders Rayevka and Bacio have something to recommend them, with two-year-old Pershaada and the improving Redorange others to throw into the mix.

View 7 Images Jane Chapple-Hyam trains Newsboy's tip (Image: Racing Photos via Getty Images)

‌



4.10 Assured Data Protection Handicap - PRIMO LARA has rediscovered his mojo - but remains well handicapped on his old form.

The chestnut son of New Bay was on the way up for Jane Chapple-Hyam in 2024, adding to a handicap-debut score at Chelmsford City in May of that year with another win in the sphere over York’s extended 10 furlongs 16 days later.

A setback led to 154 days off the track and Primo Lara lost his way, running up a 12-race losing streak for Chapple-Hyam and her Newmarket neighbour Jack Morland before coming good at Wolverhampton at the beginning of last month.

Switching from Morland back to his former trainer, the son of New Bay marked his first attempt at a mile and a half with a defeat of Masterinthewoods on Ascot’s King George VI And Queen Elizabeth undercard last time out.

‌



A 7lb rise to a British Horseracing Authority mark of 86 still leaves Primo Lara 5lb shy of his peak figure and give in the ground should not present a problem. Master Builder was back in business here in May warrants respect, along with Say What You See and Explode.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 PRIMO LARA, 2 MASTER BUILDER, 3 SAY WHAT YOU SEE

View 7 Images John (right) & Thady Gosden train Newsboy's tip (Image: PA)

4.45 British Stallion Studs EBF Convivial Maiden Stakes - LANCASTER TOWER did enough on his racecourse debut at Sandown Park last month to be of definite interest here.

‌



The colt, owned by the King and Queen and trained by John and Thady Gosden, is bred to be smart - he’s by Kingman out of the 2019 Poule d’Essai des Pouliches (French 1,000 Guineas) heroine Castle Lady.

And he must have been showing up on the Newmarket gallops - Lancaster Tower went off the 5-6 favourite to beat five opponents in Esher 23 days ago.

The result of that seven-furlong novice stakes records that my selection finished third, a length and three-quarters behind subsequent Listed winner Quest For Stars.

But Lancaster Tower travelled with menace before his lack of previous experience took its toll, and he’s expected to prove a different proposition at the second time of asking. Oklahoma, Launch Sequence and Speyside have all shown above-average ability in five races between them and are taken to fight it out for the minor medals.

‌



NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 LANCASTER TOWER, 2 LAUNCH SEQUENCE, 3 SPEYSIDE

View 7 Images Trainer Ed Walker (Image: PA)

5.20 Sky Bet EBF Fillies' Handicap - ELECTRIFARHH looks worth a try at a mile and a quarter and brings untapped potential to the table.

The daughter of Farhh is now four years old but hasn’t had much racing - she has the seventh outing of her career today.

‌



The winner of a novice stakes for fillies at Kempton Park in October 2024, Electrifarhh was limited to just one start last season, finishing second to subsequent Group 1 heroine Blue Bolt at Windsor in May 2025.

The Ed Walker trainee was entitled to need her first outing for 313 days when seventh of nine in a Kempton handicap last March and, while she couldn’t get competitive when sixth to River King at Newbury next time, there was more to like her run over a mile at Glorious Goodwood last time.

Sent off at 18-1 in a field of 14 and wearing the hold that is persevered with today, Electrifarhh and Kieran Shoemark came home with gusto to take third, beaten a nose and three-quarters of a length behind Rumba Numba.

Her finishing effort makes the step up in distance a logical move and a 2lb nudge up the weights should not prevent another decent effort. Janey Mackers, Naga and favourite Silver Lake sit at the top of a lengthy shortlist.

‌



NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 ELECTRIFARHH, 2 JANEY MACKERS, 3 SILVER LAKE

Sports.title: Michael Owen burst out crying with son's heartbreaking diagnosis 'a ticking time bomb'
Sports.content:
Michael Owen burst out crying with son's heartbreaking diagnosis 'a ticking time bomb'

Liverpool, Manchester United and England icon Michael Owen has opened up on his son's health in a new tell-all Amazon series

View 3 Images Michael Owen opens up on his personal life in the new documentary (Image: Prime Video)

Former England hero Michael Owen has opened up on his son’s “ticking time bomb” eye condition. Michael’s son, James, 20, has Stargardt, which is a rare eye disorder.

‌



The disease is inherited and causes progressive central vision loss. This usually begins in childhood or adolescence and can lead to blurry, hazy, or distorted vision.

‌



Michael, who played for Liverpool, Newcastle and Manchester United in the Premier League, admits to breaking down in tears upon learning that his son had Stargardt in his new reality series, ‘Meet the Owens’, which premieres on Amazon this week. The show gives insight into the private lives of Michael, his wife Louise, and their four children, Gemma, James, Emily, and Jessica.

‌



Talking in the show, the Liverpool icon says: “When he first got diagnosed, I remember stopping in the car, three or four times, and just bursting out crying, thinking, ‘What’s his life going to be like?’ I just wanted him to not feel sorry for himself, wanted him to have a positive outlook on life.”

James states that the condition is “like a ticking timebomb,” adding that he could go fully blind in the future. Michael also touches upon the pain and guilt he feels about James being unable to follow him into football, due to his health issues.

Arsenal dynasty predicted as one promoted team backed to survive Premier League READ MORE :

Andoni Iraola faces Liverpool problem Arne Slot couldn't solve as tactics take their toll READ MORE :

He adds: "Most people who play football have the dream of their son following in their footsteps. That’s what my dad had with me. I wanted James to be a footballer when he was really young but obviously that dream was dashed quite early.

‌



“We made James, and I don’t think I’d be normal if I didn’t put myself in the mirror and think, 'It’s down to us that he’s got this eye condition” so I did feel guilty for a little while and could say I still feel guilty now, but you look at the positives with him and the guilt sort of evaporates."

View 3 Images Michael Owen has opened up about James' health (Image: BBC)

Away from his family, Meet the Owens gives fans an unfiltered insight into Michael himself. Ultimately, his great passion is Manor House Stables, where he and his staff train and race horses.

‌



In the show, Owen says he has put “£13million to £14million” into the stables as he looks to make it one of the most successful in the industry.

Watch Michael Owen docuseries Meet the Owens for free This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more £8.99 FREE Amazon Get Amazon Prime here Product Description Amazon Prime members can watch all six episodes of Michael Owen docuseries Meet the Owens, which follows a year in the life of the former England and Liverpool striker , for free when they launch on August 28.

However, the ex-forward knows the pitfalls of the business and at one point admits that he “can’t keep haemorrhaging” money. In one scene, he tells wife Louise: “So we bought three horses today…..£273,000 we spent. Over a quarter of a million. Let’s just hang off on that new kitchen you wanted?”

‌



Michael also discusses his reputation for being, as he says in the show, “a boring p***k”, adding: “Even my kids say, 'Dad, everyone sees you as dead boring.”

However, he hits out at those who have made fun of some of his more viral moments in the past. Speaking to Simon Jordan on the latter’s Up Front podcast in December 2023, Owen discussed how competitive he was from an early age.

View 3 Images Michael Owen shows his funny side in the new show (Image: Amazon)

‌



On that podcast he said: “Everything was a challenge. I’d eat an apple watching the TV at night and the bin would be by the TV about six metres away. And I had the bravery to [throw the apple] and miss and for there to be a stain on the wallpaper. My mum would absolutely scream at me and send me upstairs."

Sports.title: Kalpana lands Yorkshire Oaks thriller but stablemate Item is team's  'first preference' for Arc
Sports.content:
Kalpana lands Yorkshire Oaks thriller but stablemate Item is team's 'first preference' for Arc

Kalpana just held on to land the Legends Global Yorkshire Oaks at York after a mighty scare from Sparan Nua in a thrilling Group One finish

View 3 Images Kalpana (left) won by a short head (Image: Richard Sellers/PA Wire)

King George heroine survived a late scare to claim the Yorkshire Oaks at York on Thursday. She was all out to thwart the dramatic late challenge of Sparan Nua in the Legends Global Yorkshire Oaks.

‌



The 10-11 favourite was made to work hard for her latest win after Aidan O'Brien's outsider Sugar Island went off in front, pulling into a 20 length lead as the field rounded the home turn.

‌



It was left to Colin Keane to chase her down from 3f out and then pass her, only for Jim Bolger's Sparan Nua – who found herself slightly hampered at one point – to eat up considerable ground and narrow the deficit.

‌



The winning post arrived just in time for Kalpana to prevail by a short head, handing Keane, Andrew Balding and owners Juddmonte a second Group One triumph within 24 hours, following Item's victory in the prestigious Juddmonte International on Wednesday.

"You knew after going a couple of furlongs it was going to be messy and passing the three (furlong marker) I thought the pacemaker was gone," said Juddmonte's European racing manager Barry Mahon.

"Colin had to commit probably a bit sooner than he wanted. When he saw himself the pacemaker was gone he had to chase her down a little bit, so she was always going to be vulnerable to something closing late, but she's gutsy and knows where the line is.

‌



View 3 Images Kalpana with the Juddmonte team at York (Image: Richard Sellers/PA Wire)

"She put her head down and got the job done. It's not pretty, but she got the job done and that's the main thing. Fast ground, slow ground, 12 furlongs - you wouldn't even be afraid to drop her back to 10. She's just very versatile and the ultimate pro now. She's fully matured now at five years of age and keeps answering all the questions, so it's wonderful."

Connections must now consider how to split their aces, with either Kalpana or Item likely to get a shot at the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe.

‌



Should Item be given the green light to head for ParisLongchamp, Kalpana - who finished seventh in last year's Arc - will almost certainly bid to win the Qipco British Champions Fillies & Mares Stakes at Ascot later in October.

Mahon added: "We have the horse from yesterday too, so whether he'll go to the Arc and we wait for Ascot with this filly - we have to sit down in a week or two and discuss all that, but it's a nice problem to have.

View 3 Images There was a very tight finish to the Yorkshire Oaks (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"The horse from yesterday has joined the fray, so we'll decide all those sort of things in the next couple of weeks with the owners and see what they want to do.

"Item is definitely a top of the ground horse. He got away with the good to soft here yesterday. Funnily enough Colin actually said this filly doesn't enjoy the softer ground as much as she did last year, he said she felt like she enjoyed the faster ground in Ascot more the last time than she did today.

"I wouldn't have thought we'd run both in the Arc. Again that will be the owners' decision, but it wouldn't be my first preference.

Article continues below

"I suppose with Item being a colt, if the ground comes up good he'd probably have the preference, and with this filly Ascot was always the target, so it would make sense to sidestep the Arc if the ground is good - but that's a big `if'.

"She probably will retire at the end of the year. Whether she'll finish at Ascot or if she doesn't go to the Arc whether she'll go to the Breeders' Cup - there's a lot of variables to work out."

Sports.title: BBC confirm Radio Norfolk plans after outrage from ITV's Ed Balls and Mark Pougatch
Sports.content:
BBC confirm Radio Norfolk plans after outrage from ITV's Ed Balls and Mark Pougatch

The BBC has issued a statement on rumoured plans to cut Norwich City away game radio coverage on BBC Radio Norfolk

View 2 Images Mark Pougatch is not happy (Image: 2025 Visionhaus)

The BBC have moved to quash claims that it intends to axe local radio coverage of Norwich City away matches on BBC Norfolk, following a wave of backlash on social media, the Mirror can reveal. A report from the Norwich Evening News had suggested that BBC bosses were plotting to cut radio coverage of Norwich's away fixtures, sparking outrage from high-profile figures including ITV's Ed Balls and Mark Pougatch.

‌



It was claimed that BBC chiefs were planning to scale back local commentaries, meaning Chris Goreham, who provides commentary for the Canaries, would only be present at home matches. A number of prominent voices waded into the row, which has since been firmly dismissed by the BBC.

‌



ITV presenter Pougatch labelled the prospect of scrapping Norwich City away game coverage 'an absolute disgrace' if the reports proved accurate. The original article suggested Norwich City supporters would be left relying on commentary from the home side's local BBC radio station as part of efforts to save millions of pounds over the next two years.

‌



Virgil van Dijk sends clear message to Liverpool owners for final days of transfer window READ MORE :

Currently, BBC Radio Norfolk dispatches both Goreham and Rob Butler to matches, alongside a former Canary who resides near the venue. However, a BBC insider has firmly denied that any alterations to local radio coverage are on the cards.

In an official statement, the corporation said: "This is not true. Home and away game commentary, analysis and coverage will continue at BBC Radio Norfolk.

"We are looking at ways to reduce duplication and showcase more of our Local commentary teams across the BBC, but no decisions have been made. Any updates will be announced in due course."

‌



View 2 Images Local radio coverage of Norwich City away games could be scrapped. (Image: Getty)

Championship outfit Norwich, who began their campaign with a 2-1 home loss to West Brom, head to Millwall next in Saturday's 12.30pm kick-off.

The reports have sparked considerable uproar on social media, with the BBC contacting local stations to clarify the rumours were unfounded, after prominent figures slammed the corporation over the allegations.

‌



Taking to social media, Pougatch said: "I am proud to say I started my career in local radio. This would be an absolute disgrace if true. Where do I sign the petition? Local football coverage is EXACTLY the sort of thing the BBC should do. No one else will!"

The ITV presenter wasn't alone in his scathing assessment of the speculation. Former Cabinet Minister and Good Morning Britain presenter Balls also weighed in.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
